about: Fixed on 2026-09-21 and not to be edited. Every stored sitting keeps
the fingerprint of this file; changing an item changes the
fingerprint, and two sittings with different fingerprints are refused
for comparison rather than misreported as progress.
If an item turns out to be bad, add exam_v2.json. The baseline is
only worth having because it did not move.

sections.instructions: Choose the option that a native speaker would say.

sections.instructions: Listen once, then answer. The audio is generated from the script when a voice is available; without one this section is skipped rather than shown as text.

items.script: So the plan changed this morning. We were going to ship the new checkout on Thursday, but legal came back with two questions about the refund flow, so now we're holding it until they sign off. Everything else in the release goes out as planned.
items.prompt: What is happening on Thursday?

items.script: I wouldn't say the migration failed exactly. It finished, but it took about four times longer than we estimated, and two of the background jobs had to be run again by hand afterwards.
items.prompt: How does the speaker describe the migration?
options: It failed and was rolled back.
It succeeded, slowly and with manual work.

items.script: Honestly, if it were up to me, I'd have gone with the managed service from the start. We'd be paying more every month, but we wouldn't have spent the last three weekends on it.
items.prompt: What is the speaker saying about the managed service?
options: They chose it and regret the cost.
They did not choose it and regret that.
They are about to migrate to it.

items.script: Just a heads up before the call: she's not going to ask you about the architecture. What she wants to know is why the incident took six hours to detect, so have that timeline ready.
items.prompt: What should the listener prepare?
options: The detection timeline for the incident.

items.script: We've been through this twice already. Every time we add a retry, the duplicate rate goes up, and every time we take it out, the support queue fills with failed payments. There isn't a version of this where we don't pick one.
items.prompt: What is the speaker's point?
options: The retry logic has a bug.
Both options have a cost and one must be chosen.
The support queue should be ignored.

items.script: Right, one last thing and then I'll let you go. The contractor's last day is the fifteenth, so anything that only he knows how to do needs to be written down or handed over before then. Not after.
items.prompt: What is the deadline for?

sections.instructions: Speak for the whole time. Do not prepare: the point is to measure what comes out unrehearsed, and a rehearsed answer in March cannot be compared with an unrehearsed one in September.

items.prompt: Describe what you worked on yesterday, from the start of the day to the end. Include something that did not go as planned.
Explain a technical decision your team made in the last year, and what you would do differently now.
You are in a job interview. Answer: what are you looking for in your next role, and why are you leaving your current one?
Disagree with this statement and defend your position: 'Code review slows teams down more than it helps them.'
